full_text:
Interviewer:	You are doing the design technology course aren’t you?

Subject:	Yes, same as [name] and [name].

Interviewer:	Yeah, did you do ‘A’ levels?

Subject:	Yes

Interviewer:	What ‘A’ levels did you do?

Subject:	I did English language, design technology and chemistry.

Interviewer:	OK, have you got any previous work experience at all?

Subject:	Hmm I did like work experience hmm from school, like for two weeks that was in a factory environment as well.

Interviewer:	OK. Are your parents in a related industry at all?

Subject:	Hmm not to design no, no.

Interviewer:	No, OK when and why do you think you decided to do design and technology at university?

Subject:	Hmm just cause I enjoy it really, and its something that I wanted to do more off so.

Interviewer:	OK did you have any careers advice or anything like that at school?

Subject:	Hmm, I had some but it wasn’t very helpful (laughs)

Interviewer:	That’s what most people have said. Did you know anyone else that was involved in the industry at all to speak to?

Subject:	Hmm only like my teachers really, hmm like one in particular was hmm quite enthusiastic so, hmm but not apart from that.

Interviewer:	OK, what attracted you to [name] University?

Subject:	Hmm I just really liked it, I thought the course seemed just exactly what I wanted and what I was looking for, I liked the university. Hmm, I thought it looked, well it is proving to be quite a good uni so.

Interviewer:	OK, when you started or before you started, did you realise that design and technology was so male dominated, was it like that at school?

Subject:	Hmm yeah pretty much, hmm, I went to an all girls school but hmm I went to like another, like comprehensive for hmm like DT and there was only a couple of girls in the whole class so, hmm yeah pretty much it.

Interviewer:	And that didn’t bother you at all?

Subject:	Hmm not really, it bothered me that we weren’t really offered it at our school but I suppose that’s more to do with the school than anything else but no, not really.

Interviewer:	Ok, so do you think that more women should be encouraged to do design and technology?

Subject:	Yeah I think so, just cause you’re a woman, doesn’t mean you don’t wanna do practical stuff so

Interviewer:	Yeah, what do you think are the advantages and disadvantages to being a woman in a male dominated environment?

Subject:	Hmm don’t know really, hmm, I suppose it shouldn’t really make much of a difference but, I don’t know, maybe I haven’t had too much experience of it yet so

Interviewer:	OK that’s fine. I’m gonna talk a bit about your course now and then about the placement. (OK) Has the degree been what you expected it to be so far?

Subject:	Hmm, yes, it’s been a bit harder than I expected. Hmm just cause it covers a lot of different areas, and yeah it’s been good.

Interviewer:	OK, what would you say has been the best and the worst things about it so far?

Subject:	Ironically probably doing a bit of everything, hmm I didn’t really expect that but I’ve quite enjoyed it. (Yeah) Hmm, I’ve started doing materials and I’ve never really done any of that before so, it’s just a chance to do something a bit different. (Yeah) Hmm the worst bits, hmm, I suppose trying to fit quite a lot into a week.

Interviewer:	Not enough time in the day?

Subject:	Yeah (laughs)

Interviewer:	OK, are you pleased that you chose this course?

Subject:	Yeah definitely.

Interviewer:	OK, have you been taught by any female lecturers at all?

Subject:	Hmm only [name] but she left. (Right ok) Hmm I suppose materials as well but that’s not really design that’s more, a slightly different department so.

Interviewer:	OK, how did you find it? Do you think you’d find it encouraging to have more female lecturers? 

Subject:	Hmm I think a little bit yeah, be nice to have a bit of variety.

Interviewer:	Yeah ok, do you think that the female lecturers that you’ve had treat you the same as the male lecturers?

Subject:	Hmm yeah I think they treat you the same, they just maybe hmm don’t instinctively go towards the boys. (Yeah) Hmm

Interviewer:	But have you found that with some of the male lecturers, do you think that?

Subject:	Hmm maybe in certain things yeah

Interviewer:	Yeah ok.

Subject:	I suppose it’s just a different perspective as well so, which is good.

Interviewer:	Yeah, have you got a personal tutor?

Subject:	Hmm, yes.

Interviewer:	Are they male or female?

Subject:	Hmm male.

Interviewer:	Have you been to see them for anything?

Subject:	Hmm yeah I have been before in the past.

Interviewer:	Do you find that they’re approachable?

Subject:	Yes really helpful

Interviewer:	You wouldn’t rather have a different personal tutor?

Subject:	Hmm not really cause I suppose its more academic problems isn’t it so not really.

Interviewer:	OK have you had to do much group work at university?

Subject:	Yeah quite a bit (laughs).

Interviewer:	Do you like doing group work or?

Subject:	Hmm yeah I don’t mind it, it’s not too bad.

Interviewer:	Have you been able to choose who you work with in groups, or do you get put with people?

Subject:	Hmm a bit of both really, I think most of the times it’s like alphabetical. (Right) But we have had some groups where we have chosen ourselves so.

Interviewer:	And how do you decide who you want to work with, do you work with your friends or?

Subject:	Yeah I tend to go with my friends if I get the chance to, so.

Interviewer:	Yeah, have you had any particularly good or bad experiences of working in groups?

Subject:	I had a particularly bad experience but that was just a personality clash I think.

Interviewer:	Was that when you were put into groups?

Subject:	Yeah actually girls against boys.

Interviewer:	OK what happened there then? 

Subject:	But hmm, it was just as I say a personality clash, somebody didn’t really want to do anything and I found it a bit unfair that we were doing all the work so yeah.

Interviewer:	OK, do you think that the university did much to help prepare you for the placement?

Subject:	No not really (laughs)

Interviewer:	OK, what do you think they could have done to help prepare you?

Subject:	Hmm I think a little bit more information, cause even now I’m not entirely sure what were meant to be handing in at the end of the year. (Yeah) Hmm even though we’ve asked, hmm, so yeah just a little bit more about what’s expected really? Hmm.

Interviewer:	Yeah, ok, were the university involved in helping find the placement for you?

Subject:	It was advertised through the department (Yeah) And people came in to give like a talk but then it was pretty much up to us to do it.

Interviewer:	OK did anyone encourage you or discourage you from going on placement at all?

Subject:	Hmm only like family and friends encouraged me really and hmm but not really in terms of lecturers, cause, I suppose they didn’t have too much to do with it so.

Interviewer:	Nobody put you off doing the placement at all then?

Subject:	Hmm people told me to think about it, but I suppose that’s a fair point. (Yeah ok) Hmm just to make sure you want to do it really.

Interviewer:	OK why did you want to go on a placement?

Subject:	Hmm the experience, bit more money (laughs) (Yeah) Hmm I think a bit more time to prepare myself in the final year as well. (Yeah) And hopefully get some ideas and a bit of experience.

Interviewer:	Ok, before you started the placement, what were you most looking forward to and maybe apprehensive about?

Subject:	Hmm I was quite looking forward to doing some design work sort of in the real world, but it hasn’t worked out like that. (Yeah) Hmm and yeah, just the chance to do something a bit different I guess. (Yeah) Something a bit more in the real world based rather than just learning about it in lectures.

Interviewer:	Yeah so that put in doing more practical instead of like the theory stuff?

Subject:	Yeah pretty much, putting into context.

Interviewer:	What attracted you to [company] then?

Subject:	Hmm it sounded like quite a good placement and they said you get to move around a bit and see different departments which we have, hmm that’s quite good cause then if there is something else other than design that you get interested in, you can pursue it a bit more. (Yeah) There’s chance to work in quite a big company as well I think so.

Interviewer:	OK how would you describe the company’s attitude to women?

Subject:	Hmm, they don’t really treat you any differently, which is fair enough. (Yeah) Hmm.

Interviewer:	OK have you found your degree work useful to the work that your doing now?

Subject:	Not probably design as design but hmm like time management, organising. (Yeah) Deadlines, that sort of thing, and communicating in groups.

Interviewer:	OK, is there anything that you wish you had learnt before you started the placement that would have helped you?

Subject:	Not really, hmm, I suppose maybe just to be a little bit more confident, but that’s probably more me rather than what I could have learnt but yeah just ask a few more questions, but I’m doing that as I go along hopefully so.

Interviewer:	OK were you taught anything about health and safety at university?

Subject:	Hmm only like in the workshops and

Interviewer:	Nothing about when you go into the workplace?

Subject:	Not really no, I suppose its, no not really.

Interviewer:	Do you think that would have been helpful or have you had plenty of that when you got here? 

Subject:	 (Laughs) Maybe there’s been quite a bit, but maybe a little bit, but again I think that could have been done maybe in some lectures as a general what to expect kind of thing so.

Interviewer:	OK before you started did either the university or your department say what they hoped that you would get from doing the placement?

Subject:	Hmm again not really, I don’t think there’s been that much guidance as such, I know they say get as much out of it as you can and try and like learn from different people and things so, yeah I guess just generally but.

Interviewer:	OK how have you found the transition from like education to work? Has it been easy or?

Subject:	 (Laughs) It’s a bit of a shock at first, hmm but I think that’s probably cause just the holiday in between as well. But yeah its not too bad, I think the most skills transfer over I guess, especially from our course, like trying to fit everything in and planning, and time management and things so yeah not too bad. 

Interviewer:	OK have you had to face any new issues at all like how to deal with different people or office politics anything like that?

Subject:	Hmm yeah, I’m learning to deal with a lot more like, the variety of people, cause like going out into the factory and things and talking to people on the line and then coming back and doing formal presentations and things so, that’s been quite useful.

Interviewer:	OK do you think that, that education experience reflects what its like in industry at all, kind of how things are structured and the work, the way that were taught, or are they two totally different situations?

Subject:	I wouldn’t say totally different but I suppose it depends where you go as well cause like small companies are obviously going to be different to like here. (Yeah) But hmm, yeah its quite different I think because especially here because they don’t really have hmm, like everybody sits together no matter what level you are, so its not really like at uni its all like staff rooms and like common rooms and things so, yeah I suppose it’s a bit more integrated here which is nice.

Interviewer:	OK, do you think that university and work have different priorities and goals?

Subject:	I suppose at uni your trying to get the best grade that you possibly can but I suppose that’s expected cause your there to do a degree at the end of the day. Hmm and I suppose really this isn’t too different cause everyone’s trying to get the best product and please customers and things, so its sort of similar.

Interviewer:	Do you think that?

Subject:	I think that’s just, this is more for the company whereas at uni its more for yourself.

Interviewer:	So uni’s more like an individual thing?

Subject:	Yeah

Interviewer:	In here it’s like a team?

Subject:	Yes it’s more of a team sort of department thing.

Interviewer:	OK can you describe the company a little bit and what they do and how big they are?

Subject:	Hmm, well it’s a massive company, there in pretty much every country.

Interviewer:	How many people work here, do you know?

Subject:	On site I think there’s a few hundred.

Interviewer:	I couldn’t believe how big it was I came in.

Subject:	 (Laughs) Yeah it is quite big.

Interviewer:	Its massive, where does it stop?

Subject:	Hmm I think its, its one of the biggest sites in Britain as well cause like we’ve been to [town] and [town] and stuff. (Yeah ) Obviously [town] is massive but hmm, like other sites are a bit smaller. (Yeah ) Hmm the office is fairly big I suppose compared to most companies, there’s a few hundred people like I say. Hmm I think it just makes it bigger here cause they’ve got the manufacturing as well. (Yeah) So … 

Interviewer:	What department are you working in?

Subject:	I’m working in research and development.

Interviewer:	OK do they employ many women in your department?

Subject:	Hmm yeah there’s a few, it’s obviously more male dominated but yeah there are some women, my boss is a woman actually.

Interviewer:	OK have [company] got a structure or programme in place for the placement students?

Subject:	Yeah when you come you get hmm like a leaflet, well it’s a booklet and its what you should work through, like every month and people try to stick pretty much to that.

Interviewer:	Do you think that’s a good idea?

Subject:	Yeah it is I think, we’ve got hmm, call it a PDP as well, its like a personal development programme hmm and you talk about with your line manager and try and decide what your goals are and what you’d like to get out of it so, and they do that for everybody though, not just us.

Interviewer:	Not just the placement students.

Subject:	So yeah it’s good.

Interviewer:	Do you think that could be improved at all? Would you change it if you was designing it?

Subject:	Hmm not really I think they’ve got it pretty much how they want it because you get to choose what you’d like to aim for and what’s relevant to your job and things so there’s quite a lot of flexibility in what you can do so its pretty good.

Interviewer:	OK hmm what does your job role involve?

Subject:	Hmm research and development (laughs) Hmm I can’t really say particularly what I’m working on. (OK, OK) Hmm, but yeah it’s just like looking at new ways maybe to do things, hmm and making sure that everything works as it’s planned.

Interviewer:	Yeah ok is that what you expected you would be doing when you got the job?

Subject:	No (laughs) I don’t really do much design at all to be fair, if any, hmm this is more like very industrial based like machines and how things work, hmm its kind of related so I can see where its going but.

Interviewer:	Is that what they told you you would be doing when you started or?

Subject:	Well we all applied for a packaging placement hmm but we obviously got put in different departments. (Yeah) I think there’s like one packaging job for how ever many people so

Interviewer:	OK, I know [name] said that you got sent quite a bit of promotional information when you, I cant remember whether its before or after your job but, do you think that that portrayed an accurate picture of the company?

Subject:	Hmm yeah the, when they recruited in our department it was all for the packaging. (Yeah) Hmm and they didn’t really say anything about the other areas.

Interviewer:	So they could have maybe just told you a bit more about that?

Subject:	Yes that could have been better but the bit about the company that was fairly accurate.

Interviewer:	OK do you feel like you’ve been given an appropriate level of responsibility?

Subject:	At first I thought maybe it wasn’t really related to my degree at all. Hmm but yeah I think its been quite good now, I’m finding that I’ve got quite a lot of responsibility, I‘m talking with people like in Europe as well and so not just here (Yeah) Hmm and then people are coming to me for answers on different things so yes, it’s quite responsible.

Interviewer:	OK you don’t feel like you’ve been given too much responsibility or?

Subject:	Hmm not really too much, not really too much hmm I suppose its quite hard because a lot of my team works abroad most of the time (Yeah) Hmm so it’s sort of getting on with it yourself. (Yeah ) Hmm but there is always back up if you need it to go and ask somebody.

Interviewer:	So you don’t feel like you’ve been left on your own?

Subject:	No not left but hmm yeah

Interviewer:	OK how would you summarise your placement experience so far then?

Subject:	Hmm its been different to what I expected, hmm at first maybe in a bit of a bad way but I think I’m enjoying it more now, hmm now I’ve got into some projects and also I’ve got a bit more responsibility, I’m not just like learning what to do.

Interviewer:	Yeah and what didn’t you like about it to begin with? 

Subject:	Hmm I think it was just trying to learn something completely different that I’d never done before in like a month or so before people were asking me what I thought of things, but again hmm I’ve been taught quite well so, I think I’ll come out with it ok and have quite a lot of different experiences.

Interviewer:	OK what would you say have been like the best and the worst things so far?

Subject:	Hmm I think some of it is a little bit repetitive what I’m doing but hmm I cant really help that cause it is like research so its kind of having a look at something, going back to it, doing it again, going back to it. Hmm I think the best things are learning totally new things which again at first I thought it was a bit bad but its quite good now I think cause I can see how I would relate it back to my course, so when I go back hopefully I’ll get a bit more of an understanding on what I’m actually do so.

Interviewer:	Yeah ok, is there anything that you thought you would achieve on your placement but you haven’t yet?

Subject:	Hmm, I thought maybe I’d be working on like a major project a little bit more, but I think I will after Christmas, cause I’ve been quite busy up until now with like team work hmm so yeah, hopefully after Christmas that should happen.

Interviewer:	OK what do you think are the main things that you’ve gained from doing the placement?

Subject:	Hmm, I think just an overview of what its like to work in a really big company (Yeah) Hmm like you say not just working for yourself, working with other people (Yeah ) And all trying to do the same thing. Cause obviously the department I’m in does its own little bit but when you get together in like a big team meeting with everybody, there’s maybe like ten different departments all around you doing the same thing so that’s quite good.

Interviewer:	OK do you think that there are any drawbacks to the placement at all?

Subject:	Hmm I think its gonna be a bit of a shock going back to uni (laughs) hmm, I quite like the nine to five, and not having anything afterwards, also maybe getting back into just working and focusing on one thing, cause at the moment I’m doing quite a few things. (Yeah) So that’s quite nice. (Yeah) Hmm but no not really.

Interviewer:	OK would you recommend other people to do a placement?

Subject:	Yeah I think so, I think so long as you get sort of something related then yeah.

Interviewer:	OK do you think that you’ve changed personally at all as a result of the placement experience?

Subject:	I think maybe I’ve got a little bit more confidence, like talking to different people (Yeah) And at first I was bit oh, I don’t know if I can but, it’s been quite good, so especially working out in the factory cause that’s quite a different environment to just sitting in an office all day so (Yeah) Yeah that’s good.

Interviewer:	OK I know that there are quite a few other placement students here, are they all male or female, what’s the sort of …

Subject:	Hmm there’s actually more girls than boys hmm, yeah there’s quite a few of us. (OK) I think there’s about nine people here and there’s two boys so.

Interviewer:	Do you think that you’re all treated equally?

Subject:	Hmm yeah I think so, I think their quite good here, they give everybody the same sort of jobs cause I took over from a male placement student who was at [university] as well, not on our course though, hmm, and I’ve pretty much taken what he left so, that’s been quite good.

Interviewer:	OK do you think its been an advantage or disadvantage having other placement students here?

Subject:	No definitely an advantage cause it’s quite nice just to talk with somebody kind of not so connected with the company (Yeah) And meet up and things so yeah it’s been good.

Interviewer:	OK do you think that you’re treated the same as the more permanent members of staff?

Subject:	Yeah definitely. Hmm you get, well you’re given the same responsibilities and you’re expected to do the same things so.

Interviewer:	Yeah ok, have you had to do quite a bit of team or group work then here?

Subject:	Hmm, yeah I’ve done quite a few like factory related things that are part of a team, hmm and then generally the work that I do gets fed back to the rest of the team so.

Interviewer:	Are there any particular people that you’ve liked or disliked working with?

Subject:	Hmm, yeah the person that I was working with at first, whose not here at the minute, but I found him really easy to get along with and I've learned a lot of the stuff that I needed to off him so that was quite good. Its nice to have someone you can get along with when you’ve got to learn quite a lot in a short space of time so (laughs). So that’s good.

Interviewer:	How do think doing teamwork at work compares to doing teamwork at university?

Subject:	I don’t know if its just cause people are getting paid and it’s like a proper job (Yeah) But people seem to be a bit more focused rather than say like with that group that just didn’t work, hmm people seem just to get on with and then like feedback to people so that’s quite good.

Interviewer:	Do you think that in the workplace when you work in groups people have got clearer roles, does everybody know what they should be doing?

Subject:	Yeah I think pretty much and also they know what’s expected of them, like right from the start and they have to deliver by a certain date so hmm yeah just more focused really. 

Interviewer:	The reason that I’m asking that is because a lot of the reason at university you’re told that you do group work is because its good practice for when you go out into the industry (Yeah) I don’t know what you think about it, if it works totally differently in the workplace then?

Subject:	Hmm I think it is a good sort of preparation but I think it is a bit different. (Yeah) Hmm I suppose cause I know you don’t really get to choose who you work with at uni sometimes either but you tend to know the people like socially as well so. (Yeah) So its quite different to just coming in and finding yourself say working with someone from Germany that you probably don’t even see when you speak to on the phone, hmm so yeah that’s a bit different.

Interviewer:	OK have you been given a mentor in the company?

Subject:	Hmm well my line, well I’ve got my line manager who kind of my mentor and hmm I’ve also got like another mentor as well that I can go to if I’ve got any problems.

Interviewer:	Yeah what do you think about that, do you think it’s a good thing or bad thing?

Subject:	Hmm yeah it’s quite a good thing especially for me cause my line manager’s away quite a bit. (Yeah) So hmm yeah, it’s been quite useful.

Interviewer:	Yeah ok, what do you think are the main benefits and drawbacks of having a mentor then?

Subject:	I think its quite good that you’ve got somebody else to go to hmm who they say is impartial but (laughs) I think it probably depends who you get, hmm but yeah, its quite nice to have somebody else to go to, just to talk to and also its like another link, cause like my mentor’s in different department, so its kind of another link to a different area in the company which is quite useful so.

Interviewer:	Are you happy with the mentor that you have, or would you rather have someone else?

Subject:	Hmm I’m fairly happy, to be fair I haven’t seen him that much hmm but that’s partly because he’s away and partly my fault but hmm, yeah it’s been quite good, its nice just as an extra back up I think.

Interviewer:	Yeah, have you ever been given any bad advice by your mentor?

Subject:	Hmm not as yet (laughs)

Interviewer:	Good, is there anyone else that you go to for advice at all?

Subject:	I think its quite good having the other IP’s here, hmm because like obviously we all meet up at lunch times and things so we tend to discuss things between ourselves really, which is quite useful. Yeah, I think that’s nice, much better than if I was just here by myself I think.

Interviewer:	Is there anyone in the company who you see as a role model at all?

Subject:	Not really (laughs)

Interviewer:	That’s fine, has anyone from the university been to visit you at all?

Subject:	Yes

Interviewer:	Yeah, why did they tell you they were coming to see you?

Subject:	Hmm we had [placement coordinator] and he didn’t spend that long, he just came to see if we was ok I guess, and have a look at our log books and things so

Interviewer:	Did he speak to your manager at all?

Subject:	No I arranged a meeting with somebody and he left before he got to speak to him which was nice (laughs)

Interviewer:	Oh ok; did you know the tutor that came to see you already?

Subject:	Hmm yeah but I haven’t, I had for like a lecture and stuff but not like on a one to basis as such. 

Interviewer:	Yeah would you be happy to go to him if you had any problems at all or would you go to someone else?

Subject:	If I had the choice I would probably go to someone else to be fair, he’s a little vague, hmm, I know we’ve asked things before about what were meant to be doing and stuff and you know he’s like oh just read the handbook which if your asking the question then obviously you need a little bit more than that.

Interviewer:	Yeah ok, are you in contact with your tutor or anyone else at uni at other times?

Subject:	Hmm not really no, I speak to like my friends and things but not really tutors.

Interviewer:	Ok, do you know if either here or the university have like a complaints procedure if you did have any problems?

Subject:	I don’t know, I guess it’s somewhere (laughs) in the book or on a leaflet or on the net somewhere, I don’t know.

Interviewer:	OK are there appropriate facilities for women here?

Subject:	Hmm yeah

Interviewer:	Yeah, I didn’t think that would apply to you but we’re interviewing engineers and so a lot are working on construction sites and stuff.

Subject:	Yeah we’ve got our own changing room and stuff so and hairdryers provided and things so yeah, seems to be pretty good.

Interviewer:	Hmm, can you think of any occasions where you feel like your gender was determined the reactions you got from people? 

Subject:	I think sometimes you get funny looks out on the line, but only because there’s not really that many women actually in the factory.

Interviewer:	They’re just surprised to see a woman?

Subject:	Yeah well I suppose like a new face more than anything, hmm cause like the women that are already there obviously just sort of joke around and blend in so I suppose some one new, hmm no.

Interviewer:	Do you get on all right with them?

Subject:	Yeah seem to, hmm they seem to be quite helpful, maybe its just because I’m, I seem not to know what I’m doing sometimes, but everyone seems to be really helpful. (Yeah ) If you just ask then, its good. The only problem hmm I sometimes get is if I’m not like tall enough to reach something or hmm its sort of the factory is built for men I think.

Interviewer:	Right, ok, that’s interesting.

Subject:	But yeah, I suppose they cant really help that but hmm yeah, sometimes if I’m asked to do something, its like I would but I really cannot reach (laughs).

Interviewer:	Do you want a career in design and technology?

Subject:	Hmm, I don’t think I’d want to work for a design consultancy as such, but I’d like to do something related, I’m not exactly sure what yet but

Interviewer:	OK do you think that you’d like to go into a more managerial role or maybe sort of a technical or specialist?

Subject:	Hmm I think maybe technical well sort of specialist, technical. Hmm I quite enjoy what I’m doing at the moment; I’d like to maybe do something a little bit different but the same sort of area so. Yeah the development sides quite good.

Interviewer:	OK do you think that the career prospects are good in design and technology?

Subject:	Hmm I think maybe jobs are a bit more difficult to find than some other areas, probably more competitive as well. 

Interviewer:	What about once you get in to the industry, like prospects for promotion and things like that? 

Subject:	Hmm I suppose it depends what company your in cause I know like here, if you really want to be promoted then there’s quite a few avenues you can go through, hmm, I don’t really know how that would fare if you were, wanted just design promotion sort of thing. 

Interviewer:	Yeah, ok, do you think that your career ambitions have changed at all as a result of doing the placement?

Subject:	No I probably don’t want to work with pet food again, but hmm I think maybe a little bit cause I’d like to do something a bit more specialist like I say rather than really vague. (Yeah) But yeah

Interviewer:	Would you work for the company if they offered you a job when you finish?

Subject:	Maybe if I was doing a different role to what I’m doing now, I don’t know if I’d like to do this for the next 20 odd years but maybe something kind of related.

Interviewer:	OK do you think that the placement will help you when you start work after uni?

Subject:	Yeah I think so. I think its quite good to have some experience. Hmm and to sort of know what I’m going into.

Interviewer:	Do you think it’ll be useful even if you go into a different area?

Subject:	Yeah I think so, cause it’s the same sort of skills like talking to people and getting things done and communication and things so yeah I think it’ll be quite useful. I think it’ll be useful when I go back to uni as well. Just like say the time management things hmm like just getting everything done and then planning stuff like that so yeah.

Interviewer:	Do you think it will help you do your final year project and things like that as well?

Subject:	I think I’ll be a lot more organised, hmm cause I know I definitely am now to what I was like last year and when I started, hmm, just simple things like getting up really early and making thing sure that everything’s all ready and stuff so yeah I think definitely, from that side it’ll be quite helpful.

Interviewer:	OK are you happy with all your career choices that you made so far, would you do anything differently if you started over again?

Subject:	Hmm I’m quite glad I chose the course that I did, hmm I think I would do a placement again hmm I don’t know, maybe I probably would have looked for something a little bit more related to my course. But its still not a bad placement so, hmm no I don’t think I would have made any different decisions.

turns.text: Are there any particular people that you’ve liked or disliked working with?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm, yeah the person that I was working with at first, whose not here at the minute, but I found him really easy to get along with and I've learned a lot of the stuff that I needed to off him so that was quite good. Its nice to have someone you can get along with when you’ve got to learn quite a lot in a short space of time so (laughs). So that’s good.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: How do think doing teamwork at work compares to doing teamwork at university?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I don’t know if its just cause people are getting paid and it’s like a proper job (Yeah) But people seem to be a bit more focused rather than say like with that group that just didn’t work, hmm people seem just to get on with and then like feedback to people so that’s quite good.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think that in the workplace when you work in groups people have got clearer roles, does everybody know what they should be doing?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah I think pretty much and also they know what’s expected of them, like right from the start and they have to deliver by a certain date so hmm yeah just more focused really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: The reason that I’m asking that is because a lot of the reason at university you’re told that you do group work is because its good practice for when you go out into the industry (Yeah) I don’t know what you think about it, if it works totally differently in the workplace then?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm I think it is a good sort of preparation but I think it is a bit different. (Yeah) Hmm I suppose cause I know you don’t really get to choose who you work with at uni sometimes either but you tend to know the people like socially as well so. (Yeah) So its quite different to just coming in and finding yourself say working with someone from Germany that you probably don’t even see when you speak to on the phone, hmm so yeah that’s a bit different.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK have you been given a mentor in the company?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm well my line, well I’ve got my line manager who kind of my mentor and hmm I’ve also got like another mentor as well that I can go to if I’ve got any problems.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah what do you think about that, do you think it’s a good thing or bad thing?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm yeah it’s quite a good thing especially for me cause my line manager’s away quite a bit. (Yeah) So hmm yeah, it’s been quite useful.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah ok, what do you think are the main benefits and drawbacks of having a mentor then?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think its quite good that you’ve got somebody else to go to hmm who they say is impartial but (laughs) I think it probably depends who you get, hmm but yeah, its quite nice to have somebody else to go to, just to talk to and also its like another link, cause like my mentor’s in different department, so its kind of another link to a different area in the company which is quite useful so.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Are you happy with the mentor that you have, or would you rather have someone else?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm I’m fairly happy, to be fair I haven’t seen him that much hmm but that’s partly because he’s away and partly my fault but hmm, yeah it’s been quite good, its nice just as an extra back up I think.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah, have you ever been given any bad advice by your mentor?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm not as yet (laughs)

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Good, is there anyone else that you go to for advice at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think its quite good having the other IP’s here, hmm because like obviously we all meet up at lunch times and things so we tend to discuss things between ourselves really, which is quite useful. Yeah, I think that’s nice, much better than if I was just here by myself I think.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Is there anyone in the company who you see as a role model at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Not really (laughs)

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: That’s fine, has anyone from the university been to visit you at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah, why did they tell you they were coming to see you?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm we had [placement coordinator] and he didn’t spend that long, he just came to see if we was ok I guess, and have a look at our log books and things so

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Did he speak to your manager at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: No I arranged a meeting with somebody and he left before he got to speak to him which was nice (laughs)

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Oh ok; did you know the tutor that came to see you already?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm yeah but I haven’t, I had for like a lecture and stuff but not like on a one to basis as such.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah would you be happy to go to him if you had any problems at all or would you go to someone else?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: If I had the choice I would probably go to someone else to be fair, he’s a little vague, hmm, I know we’ve asked things before about what were meant to be doing and stuff and you know he’s like oh just read the handbook which if your asking the question then obviously you need a little bit more than that.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah ok, are you in contact with your tutor or anyone else at uni at other times?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm not really no, I speak to like my friends and things but not really tutors.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok, do you know if either here or the university have like a complaints procedure if you did have any problems?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I don’t know, I guess it’s somewhere (laughs) in the book or on a leaflet or on the net somewhere, I don’t know.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK are there appropriate facilities for women here?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm yeah

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah, I didn’t think that would apply to you but we’re interviewing engineers and so a lot are working on construction sites and stuff.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah we’ve got our own changing room and stuff so and hairdryers provided and things so yeah, seems to be pretty good.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Hmm, can you think of any occasions where you feel like your gender was determined the reactions you got from people?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think sometimes you get funny looks out on the line, but only because there’s not really that many women actually in the factory.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: They’re just surprised to see a woman?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah well I suppose like a new face more than anything, hmm cause like the women that are already there obviously just sort of joke around and blend in so I suppose some one new, hmm no.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you get on all right with them?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah seem to, hmm they seem to be quite helpful, maybe its just because I’m, I seem not to know what I’m doing sometimes, but everyone seems to be really helpful. (Yeah ) If you just ask then, its good. The only problem hmm I sometimes get is if I’m not like tall enough to reach something or hmm its sort of the factory is built for men I think.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Right, ok, that’s interesting.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: But yeah, I suppose they cant really help that but hmm yeah, sometimes if I’m asked to do something, its like I would but I really cannot reach (laughs).

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you want a career in design and technology?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm, I don’t think I’d want to work for a design consultancy as such, but I’d like to do something related, I’m not exactly sure what yet but

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK do you think that you’d like to go into a more managerial role or maybe sort of a technical or specialist?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm I think maybe technical well sort of specialist, technical. Hmm I quite enjoy what I’m doing at the moment; I’d like to maybe do something a little bit different but the same sort of area so. Yeah the development sides quite good.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK do you think that the career prospects are good in design and technology?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm I think maybe jobs are a bit more difficult to find than some other areas, probably more competitive as well.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: What about once you get in to the industry, like prospects for promotion and things like that?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm I suppose it depends what company your in cause I know like here, if you really want to be promoted then there’s quite a few avenues you can go through, hmm, I don’t really know how that would fare if you were, wanted just design promotion sort of thing.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah, ok, do you think that your career ambitions have changed at all as a result of doing the placement?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: No I probably don’t want to work with pet food again, but hmm I think maybe a little bit cause I’d like to do something a bit more specialist like I say rather than really vague. (Yeah) But yeah

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Would you work for the company if they offered you a job when you finish?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Maybe if I was doing a different role to what I’m doing now, I don’t know if I’d like to do this for the next 20 odd years but maybe something kind of related.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK do you think that the placement will help you when you start work after uni?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah I think so. I think its quite good to have some experience. Hmm and to sort of know what I’m going into.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think it’ll be useful even if you go into a different area?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah I think so, cause it’s the same sort of skills like talking to people and getting things done and communication and things so yeah I think it’ll be quite useful. I think it’ll be useful when I go back to uni as well. Just like say the time management things hmm like just getting everything done and then planning stuff like that so yeah.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think it will help you do your final year project and things like that as well?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think I’ll be a lot more organised, hmm cause I know I definitely am now to what I was like last year and when I started, hmm, just simple things like getting up really early and making thing sure that everything’s all ready and stuff so yeah I think definitely, from that side it’ll be quite helpful.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK are you happy with all your career choices that you made so far, would you do anything differently if you started over again?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm I’m quite glad I chose the course that I did, hmm I think I would do a placement again hmm I don’t know, maybe I probably would have looked for something a little bit more related to my course. But its still not a bad placement so, hmm no I don’t think I would have made any different decisions.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Someone else said that you could maybe have done with more advice in that sense on your course like, I think [company] were one of the sort of first companies that you heard about …

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah pretty much

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: And then that they would have liked some more advice on what to do when you sort of get offered a job …

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yeah cause you kind of think (laughs), yeah this was quite early on hmm and I suppose its always that thing of, well I take it and hope nothing better comes along or I don’t and I lose it and I get nothing. (Yeah) So, hmm yeah I think from that perspective, it would have been nicer to have a few more choices at one time rather than like one a few months ahead of everything else.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK, what five words would you use to describe the culture and the characteristics of either the design and technology industry generally or more specific the work that you’ve been doing?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: What I’ve been doing here? (Yeah) Hmm I’d say its quite challenging, there’s quite a few hmm like not so much problems but things that have to solved and solved quickly. So yeah challenging, I think quite varied as well, cause it’s amazing how many different areas work on the same tiny little thing. (Yeah) I suppose design is quite competitive (Yeah) You don’t really find that so much here but I suppose its cause I’m not really working in design as such. Hmm I don’t know really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Would you describe it as masculine or male dominated?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Hmm I think it is definitely more male dominated but it doesn’t always make much of a difference (Yeah) So I don’t know if that would change if I worked here for a long time or if like I tried to get higher in the company or go into different areas, I don’t know so.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yeah, yeah, why do you think that design and technology is male dominated?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: From my perspective maybe just because its not really advertised to girls as much cause I know definitely from my school it was never offered as an A level option and then we were like the first year to ask for it (Yeah) So I think it is now but, for us that was kind of a bit too late so. (Yeah) Hmmm yeah I think maybe just cause its not really advertised as such so.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK hmm that’s everything then. Thank you very much.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: That’s ok

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: That’s been very helpful.
